result.summary: This PR raises Bitcoin Core's minimum supported GCC version from 12 to 13, primarily to enable use of std::format in new code and to pave the way toward requiring C++23 later. It updates dependencies.md, adds a CMake compile-time check enforcing the new minimum, updates many CI environment scripts (including a mechanical refactor to printf %q-based quoting), and adds NetBSD cross-compilation toolchain support for a newer GCC. It also converts one benchmark (wallet_migration.cpp) from tinyformat to std::format as an example.
result.problem: Developers cannot use std::format in new C++ code until the minimum compiler is raised, and the project wants to prepare for a future C++23 requirement; this affects contributors writing new code and the release engineering process, not end users directly.

open_concerns: How to handle NetBSD cross-compilation CI: the author is unsure whether to keep coverage that doesn't reflect a real native NetBSD user setup, since NetBSD's native GCC differs from the cross toolchain (maflcko, fanquake, hebasto discussion)
hebasto identified linker warnings (libstdc++ version conflicts) when using a newer GCC natively on NetBSD, deemed likely harmless but unconfirmed
Build documentation for NetBSD users installing a newer GCC has not been written yet, per fanquake's suggestion

result.card: This PR bumps Bitcoin Core's minimum supported GCC version from 12 to 13, primarily to enable std::format in new code and to prepare for a future C++23 requirement, alongside a mechanical CI quoting refactor and NetBSD cross-toolchain updates. The change is release-scoped for 2027 (33.x) per the author, so it carries no urgency, but it has leverage: related PRs #36033 (C++23 requirement) and #36036 (clang 19 bump) build on or conflict with it. The PR is a draft, explicitly because the author is stuck on an open design question about how to represent NetBSD cross-compilation coverage in CI, since native NetBSD needs a non-default newer GCC; this has been unresolved and the author silent since 2026-08-24. hebasto gave a Concept ACK and contributed detailed NetBSD testing notes, but no consensus on the CI approach has been reached, and the PR needs a rebase.
